🙄 Everyone is tired of AI. Unpopular opinion: we're not tired, we're early.

About half of adults now use AI chatbots, but fewer than 1 in 10 are real power users. Most of us use it like Google: a short question, the first answer, done. Generic question in, generic answer out. Same with images: "woman in a café" gets you a plastic face.

· AI runs on context: who you are + what you want + the details
· Same app, two people, completely different results (card 4)
· Where are you on the stairs? (card 5)
· Try the prompt on card 7 tonight and compare the two answers

✍️ One sentence isn't a prompt. Here's how to build one, and why it works.

"Plan my weekend" gets you a museum, a restaurant and a walk in the park. That's not AI being bad: every gap you leave, it fills with the most average guess.

Build your prompt in four parts:
· Who I am, so it stops guessing who it's for
· What I want, so it knows the actual job
· The details, so it fits your real life (budget, time, weather, what you love)
· How I want it, so you get it in a shape you can use

Then reply instead of starting over: "shorter", "more like me", "3 options".

🧡 ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini? Here's which one I actually use.

Three apps, one idea: you type, they answer. The difference is in the details.

· ChatGPT (OpenAI): the famous all-rounder
· Claude (Anthropic): my everyday assistant
· Gemini (Google): best if you live in Gmail and Docs

I use ChatGPT and Claude, but now mainly Claude. Everything I show you here is a real Claude example, so if you want to follow along, use Claude.

Free or paid? Free is fine for a question or two a day. If AI is part of your work and your day, pay for it. I use Claude Pro.

🗺️ Six buttons. That's the whole of Claude.

The first time I opened it, the left side looked like a cockpit. It isn't. Here's what each button does, in plain words:

· New: a blank chat, write like you'd brief a colleague
· Search: find any old chat in seconds
· Projects: one desk per area of your life
· Artifacts: the documents, slides and sheets it makes you
· Scheduled: tasks that run on their own (paid plans)
· Customize: connect your apps and teach it your way

Plus the same Claude on your phone, with the same chats.

🪞 The Claude setting most people never open.

Every new chat starts with a stranger, so most of us keep typing "I'm a project manager, I have two kids…" again and again. There's a box where you write it once, and Claude reads it before every chat.

· Where: your name (bottom left) → Settings → Your Claude → Instructions (card 2 shows the clicks)
· What to write: two parts, who you are + how you like answers
· Don't know what to write? Card 6 has a prompt where Claude interviews you and writes it for you
· Never put passwords, ID numbers or health details there

🎙️ Stop typing to Claude. Start talking.

Most people only use the text field. There are four buttons hiding in the Claude chat box, and one of them lets you just talk: ramble, pause, restart, and it types it all out for you.

· Mic: press it and speak, messy is fine (card 2)
· Plus: files, folders and your apps behind one button (card 3)
· The model menu: which one when, with real examples (cards 4–5)
   Haiku for quick answers, Sonnet for simple tasks, Opus for everyday and complex work, Fable for the toughest jobs
· Effort: Medium for most days, go higher only for the important stuff (card 6)

🧡 Is it AI? Look closer.

Yes, she's AI. But she doesn't look fake, and that's not luck. Most AI portraits look plastic because they're too perfect. Real faces have texture, and AI only adds it when you describe it.

· Eyes: soft window catchlight, separate lashes
· Fabric: loose mohair fibres catching the light
· Skin: visible pores, uneven freckles, no smoothing
· Lips: fine lines, matte, never glossy
· Hair: flyaways and baby hairs

🔌 Still copy-pasting emails into AI? There's a shortcut.

Connectors give Claude a key to one of your apps, so it can look things up there itself, only when you ask.

· Calendar: find a slot when all four of you are free
· Gmail: what did the landlord say about the deposit?
· Drive: summarise the Q3 report in five bullets
· Canva: turn text into a post draft

Drive, Gmail and Calendar work on the free plan. Claude asks before it sends or deletes anything.

💎 Your prompt is a gemstone. The more you polish it, the more it shines.

"A woman with an orange ring" is a rough stone: you get a shiny stock-photo ring and plastic skin. Every detail you add is one more cut.

· Cut 1, the stone: name exactly what you want (emerald-cut orange sapphire, double claw prongs, diamond side stones)
· Cut 2, the light: soft window light, real skin texture, fine lines on the knuckles
· Cut 3, the shot: extreme close-up, shallow depth of field, luxury editorial

More work, more shine. My fill-in template is on card 7, and it works for any product photo. Save it for your next shoot.

✨ Don't just chat with AI. Make something.

An artifact is a real thing Claude makes for you: a document, a slide deck, a spreadsheet, even a small app. It opens next to the chat, and you can edit, download or share it.

· Doc: the meeting summary your boss actually reads
· Slides: the five-slide pitch for your side project
· Sheet: the Christmas gift budget with totals
· App: a tiny habit tracker

🧳 I found a hotel in Madrid without opening a single tab.

One message to Claude: city, date, budget, breakfast. It searched Booking.com for me and came back with real hotels, photos, ratings and prices, all under budget and with breakfast included.

· Connect Booking.com once in Customize → Connectors, then switch it on with + → Connectors
· Put every detail in one message: city, dates, nights, budget, breakfast, area
· Claude asks before it uses the app; you press Allow once
· You still read the reviews and press book yourself

My exact prompt is on card 5. Save it for your next trip and send this to your travel buddy.

📸 4 words that make AI photos look editorial, not AI.

AI defaults to the safest picture: centred, frozen, evenly lit. One mood word breaks that default.

· Sculptural: one bold shape, nothing else
· Wind: hair and fabric caught mid-moment
· Motion blur: the photo that looks like a feeling
· Close & still: tight crop, direct gaze, total calm

The exact phrases are on each card, and the full template is on card 5. Save it for your next shoot.

⏰ The AI task that runs while you're in the bath.

A scheduled task is a prompt you write once, and Claude runs it on its own every day or week, even with your laptop closed (paid plans).

· Monday 8:00: plan my week from my calendar
· Friday 16:00: draft my update for my manager
· 1st of the month: bills and renewals
· Sunday: five dinners and one shopping list

Mine: every Monday my strategist Lou drafts my content week, and twice a week a trends report lands. The Friday-update prompt is on card 5.

🧠 Teach Claude once. Get it right every time.

A skill saves your way of working as a recipe: your steps, your rules, your style. Next time you just say "write my Friday update".

· Pick a task you repeat every week
· Do it once in a chat until it's exactly right
· Say: "turn this into a skill"

My AI team is three skills: Lou plans my content, Mila edits my videos and Remy designed this carousel. The prompt to build your first one is on card 5. Works on the free plan too.

🔍 Small details, big difference.

The first picture was good enough. Pretty, even. But look closer: smooth skin, no freckles, glossy lips, soft lashes. It looks a little like a filter.

So I didn't start over. I sent one more message and asked for the small things:
· visible pores and light freckles
· fine lines on the lips, natural matte finish
· individual lashes of uneven length
· separate hair strands, no skin smoothing

👻 The chat Claude forgets.

Click the little ghost on a new chat and you're incognito: it isn't saved to your history, isn't used for memory and isn't used to train Claude.

· The salary question before your review
· The health question you feel silly asking
· Your partner's gift, on a shared laptop

Honest part: incognito chats are still kept for 30 days for safety, then deleted. Private, not a vault, so passwords and card numbers never go in any chat.

The salary prompt is on card 6. Available on every plan, including free.

👢 These boots don't exist. I imagined them.

Orange fluffy boots with black polka dots: a silly idea in my head, a real-looking photo a minute later. Then I put them on a tree, just to see.

That's the part of AI nobody talks about enough: whatever comes into your mind, you can see it before it exists.
· a product idea before you make it
· your living room in a new colour
· that dress, but in your colour and length
